subproblems.title: At Hⁿ-a.e. point, a positive integer mass density k forces carrier membership with multiplicity k
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) be a current on U = ℝ^P (GeometricCurrentOn univ n) and let R = (M, θ, ξ) ∈ IMRep(ℝ^P, n) represent C (R.Represents C). Then for μHE[n]-almost every y ∈ ℝ^P the following holds: for every k ∈ ℕ with k ≥ 1, if HasMassDensity C y k (i.e. M_{B_ρ(y)}(C)/(ω_n ρ^n) → k as ρ ↓ 0), then y ∈ M and θ(y) = k.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), R.Represents C → ∀ᵐ y ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Euclid P)), ∀ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k → HasMassDensity C y k → y ∈ R.carrier ∧ R.mult y = k
subproblems.natural_proof:
Notation and used results. H^n := μHE[n] on ℝ^P = Euclid P; M := R.carrier; θ := R.mult; μ := R.measure = (H^n.restrict M).withDensity (fun x => (θ x : ℝ≥0∞)); ω_n := unitBallVolume n; B_s(x) := ball x s and B̄_s(x) := closedBall x s. Sibling reuse children (comparator-accepted declarations, used at their frozen types): mass_eq_measure = Submission.rsd_massOn_eq_measure (IsOpen U → R.Represents T → ∀ W, IsOpen W → W ⊆ U → T.massOn W = R.measure W); ae_density_mult = Submission.rsd_ae_hasMassDensity_mult (IsOpen U → R.Represents T → ∀ᵐ x ∂R.measure, HasMassDensity T x (R.mult x)); lower_density_comparison = Submission.dorag_sn_hausdorff_le_mul_of_lower_density (∀ (N n : ℕ) (c : ℝ), 0 < c → ∃ C : ℝ≥0∞, C ≠ ∞ ∧ ∀ (ν : Measure (Euclid N)) (A O : Set (Euclid N)), IsOpen O → A ⊆ O → (∀ x ∈ A, ∃ t₀ : ℝ, 0 < t₀ ∧ ∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → t < t₀ → ENNReal.ofReal (c * t ^ n) ≤ ν (closedBall x t)) → μHE[n] A ≤ C * ν O); null_open_superset = Submission.dorag_sn_open_superset_measure_lt (∀ (N : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid N)) (A : Set (Euclid N)), μ A = 0 → (∀ x ∈ A, ∃ r : ℝ, 0 < r ∧ μ (ball x r) ≠ ∞) → ∀ ε : ℝ≥0∞, 0 < ε → ∃ O : Set (Euclid N), IsOpen O ∧ A ⊆ O ∧ μ O < ε). This is the classical argument behind Θ^n(μ_T, ·) = θ·1_M H^n-a.e. (Simon, Ch. 3, Remark 1.8; Ch. 1, Theorem 3.3).
1. (Mass equals weight.) mass_eq_measure with U := univ (isOpen_univ, hR) gives C.massOn W = μ W for every open W; in particular C.massOn (B_s(x)) = μ (B_s(x)) for all x and s.
2. (Density on the carrier.) ae_density_mult with U := univ gives: for μ-a.e. x, HasMassDensity C x θ(x). The density fun x => (θ x : ℝ≥0∞) is measurable (R.measurable_mult composed with the cast, `measurable_from_nat`), so `ae_withDensity_iff` rewrites this as: for (H^n.restrict M)-a.e. x, (θ x : ℝ≥0∞) ≠ 0 → HasMassDensity C x θ(x); and `ae_restrict_iff'` (R.measurableSet_carrier) as: for H^n-a.e. x, x ∈ M → (θ x : ℝ≥0∞) ≠ 0 → HasMassDensity C x θ(x). For x ∈ M we have θ x > 0 (R.mult_pos), so (θ x : ℝ≥0∞) ≠ 0. Hence (E_on): for H^n-a.e. y, y ∈ M → HasMassDensity C y θ(y).
3. (Constants and local finiteness.) ω_n ≠ 0 (`measure_ball_pos volume (0 : Euclid n) one_pos`) and ω_n ≠ ∞ (`measure_ball_ne_top`). For every x, μ(B_1(x)) ≤ μ(B̄_1(x)) = ∫⁻ z in M ∩ B̄_1(x), (θ z : ℝ≥0∞) ∂H^n (`withDensity_apply` and `Measure.restrict_restrict` for the closed ball, then `Set.inter_comm`), which is ≠ ∞ by R.locallyIntegrable_mult applied to the compact set B̄_1(x) ⊆ univ.
4. (The off-carrier set is μ-null.) Let A := {y | y ∉ M ∧ ∃ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k ∧ HasMassDensity C y k}. Then (H^n.restrict M)(A) = H^n(A ∩ M) (`Measure.restrict_apply'`, M measurable) = H^n(∅) = 0, because A ∩ M = ∅. Since μ ≪ H^n.restrict M (`withDensity_absolutelyContinuous`), μ(A) = 0.
5. (Uniform lower density on A.) Put t := 1/2 and c := t · ω_n.toReal; then c > 0 by Step 3 (`ENNReal.toReal_pos`). Let x ∈ A, with k ≥ 1 and HasMassDensity C x k. Since t < 1 ≤ k we have ofReal t < ofReal k, so Ioi (ofReal t) is a neighbourhood of ofReal k; the second component of HasMassDensity C x k and `mem_nhdsGT_iff_exists_Ioo_subset` give t₀ > 0 with ofReal t < C.massOn (B_s(x)) / (ω_n · ofReal (s^n)) for every s ∈ (0, t₀). For such s the denominator d := ω_n · ofReal (s^n) is ≠ 0 (s^n > 0) and ≠ ∞, so `ENNReal.le_div_iff_mul_le` gives ofReal (c · s^n) = ofReal t · d ≤ C.massOn (B_s(x)) (the equality by `ENNReal.ofReal_mul` and `ENNReal.ofReal_toReal`). By Step 1 and monotonicity, C.massOn (B_s(x)) = μ(B_s(x)) ≤ μ(B̄_s(x)). So every x ∈ A has t₀ > 0 with ofReal (c · s^n) ≤ μ(B̄_s(x)) for all s ∈ (0, t₀).
6. (Comparison.) lower_density_comparison with (N := P, n, c) gives K : ℝ≥0∞ with K ≠ ∞ such that, applied with ν := μ, any open O ⊇ A and the lower bound of Step 5, H^n(A) ≤ K · μ(O).
7. (Small open neighbourhoods.) Let ε > 0. null_open_superset applied to μ and A (μ(A) = 0 by Step 4; each x ∈ A has μ(B_1(x)) ≠ ∞ by Step 3, take r := 1) gives an open O ⊇ A with μ(O) < ε. By Step 6, H^n(A) ≤ K · μ(O) ≤ K · ε.
8. (A is H^n-null.) For j ∈ ℕ, ε := (j : ℝ≥0∞)⁻¹ > 0 (`ENNReal.inv_pos`, (j : ℝ≥0∞) ≠ ∞), so H^n(A) ≤ K · (j : ℝ≥0∞)⁻¹; and K · (j : ℝ≥0∞)⁻¹ → 0 as j → ∞ because K ≠ ∞ (`ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul` with `ENNReal.tendsto_inv_nat_nhds_zero`). Hence H^n(A) = 0 (`ge_of_tendsto'`), i.e. (E_off): for H^n-a.e. y, y ∉ A (`measure_eq_zero_iff_ae_notMem`).
9. (Conclusion.) Fix y satisfying E_on and E_off, and k ∈ ℕ with 1 ≤ k and HasMassDensity C y k. If y ∉ M, then y ∈ A (witness k), contradicting E_off; so y ∈ M. By E_on, HasMassDensity C y θ(y). Both density statements are limits of the same function ρ ↦ C.massOn (B_ρ(y)) / (ω_n · ofReal (ρ^n)) along the nontrivial filter 𝓝[>] 0, so `tendsto_nhds_unique` gives ofReal (k : ℝ) = ofReal (θ(y) : ℝ). Both reals are ≥ 0, so (k : ℝ) = θ(y) (`ENNReal.ofReal_eq_ofReal_iff`), hence θ(y) = k (cast injectivity, `exact_mod_cast`). Thus y ∈ R.carrier ∧ R.mult y = k, for H^n-a.e. y and every such k. ∎
proof_key_steps: mass_eq_measure gives C.massOn(B_s(x)) = μ(B_s(x)); ae_density_mult, ae_withDensity_iff, ae_restrict_iff' and θ ≥ 1 on M give HasMassDensity C y θ(y) for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ M.
The off-carrier set A := {y ∉ M : ∃ k ≥ 1, HasMassDensity C y k} is μ-null (A ∩ M = ∅, μ ≪ Hⁿ⌞M) and satisfies ofReal(ω_n s^n/2) ≤ μ(B̄_s(x)) for small s at each x ∈ A.
lower_density_comparison gives Hⁿ(A) ≤ K·μ(O) for every open O ⊇ A; null_open_superset makes μ(O) < ε, so Hⁿ(A) = 0.
Off A, density k ≥ 1 forces y ∈ M, and uniqueness of limits along 𝓝[>] 0 gives θ(y) = k.

subproblems.title: On a relatively open flat region of density k, almost every point is a carrier point with multiplicity k and approximate tangent plane Q
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n), Q ⊆ ℝ^P a linear subspace with dim Q = n, G ⊆ ℝ^P an arbitrary set, k ∈ ℕ with k ≥ 1, and R = (M, θ, ξ) ∈ IMRep(ℝ^P, n) with R.Represents C. Assume every y ∈ G satisfies: y ∈ Q, HasMassDensity C y k, and there is r > 0 with Q ∩ B_r(y) ⊆ G and spt C ∩ B_r(y) ⊆ Q. Then for μHE[n]-a.e. y ∈ ℝ^P: if y ∈ G, then y ∈ M, θ(y) = k and approxTangentPlane n M y = Q.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (G : Set (Euclid P)) (k : ℕ) (R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), Module.finrank ℝ Q = n → 1 ≤ k → (∀ y ∈ G, y ∈ Q ∧ HasMassDensity C y k ∧ ∃ r : ℝ, 0 < r ∧ (Q : Set (Euclid P)) ∩ ball y r ⊆ G ∧ C.support ∩ ball y r ⊆ (Q : Set (Euclid P))) → R.Represents C → ∀ᵐ y ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Euclid P)), y ∈ G → y ∈ R.carrier ∧ R.mult y = k ∧ approxTangentPlane n R.carrier y = Q
subproblems.natural_proof:
Notation and used results. H^n := μHE[n]; M := R.carrier; θ := R.mult; spt C := C.support; (hG) is the hypothesis on G. Siblings: density_mult = Submission.idtp_cse_sp_density_mult_ae (R.Represents C → ∀ᵐ y ∂μHE[n], ∀ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k → HasMassDensity C y k → y ∈ R.carrier ∧ R.mult y = k); reuse child carrier_support_null = Submission.imrep_carrier_sdiff_support_null (IsOpen U → R.Represents T → μHE[n] (R.carrier \ T.support) = 0); reuse child approx_tangent_null_diff = Submission.dtc_approxTangent_of_null_diff (M' ⊆ M → IsOpen V → x ∈ V → μHE[n] ((M \ M') ∩ V) = 0 → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' x Q). From the SimonGMT library of the frozen contract: `Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.hasApproximateTangentSpaceAt_submodule` (finrank ℝ Q = n → x ∈ Q → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (Q : Set _) x Q) and `HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique` (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(1)).
1. (Membership and multiplicity a.e. on G.) density_mult applied to (P, n, C, R, hR) gives: for H^n-a.e. y, every k' ≥ 1 with HasMassDensity C y k' satisfies y ∈ M ∧ θ y = k'. For y ∈ G, (hG) gives HasMassDensity C y k with 1 ≤ k. Hence (E1): for H^n-a.e. y, y ∈ G → (y ∈ M ∧ θ y = k).
2. (G \ M is H^n-null.) By `ae_iff`, E1 says H^n {y | ¬(y ∈ G → y ∈ M ∧ θ y = k)} = 0. Every y ∈ G \ M lies in this set (y ∈ G but y ∉ M). By `measure_mono_null`, (E2): H^n (G \ M) = 0.
3. (Approximate tangent planes a.e. on M.) The structure field R.orients says: for (H^n.restrict M)-a.e. y there is T with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M y T (and an orientation property, which is discarded). As M is measurable (R.measurableSet_carrier), `ae_restrict_iff'` turns this into (E3): for H^n-a.e. y, y ∈ M → ∃ T, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M y T.
4. (M lies a.e. in spt C.) carrier_support_null applied to (P, n, univ, C, R, isOpen_univ, hR) gives (E4): H^n (M \ spt C) = 0.
5. (Pointwise argument.) Combine E1 and E3 (filter_upwards), fix y satisfying both, and assume y ∈ G. By E1, y ∈ M and θ y = k; by E3 choose T with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M y T. By (hG), y ∈ Q and there is r > 0 with Q ∩ ball y r ⊆ G and spt C ∩ ball y r ⊆ Q. Let V := ball y r (open, and y ∈ V because r > 0) and M' := M ∩ Q.
   (i) (M \ M') ∩ V ⊆ M \ spt C: if z ∈ M, z ∉ M ∩ Q, z ∈ V and z ∈ spt C, then z ∈ spt C ∩ ball y r ⊆ Q, so z ∈ M ∩ Q, a contradiction. By E4 and `measure_mono_null`, H^n ((M \ M') ∩ V) = 0. approx_tangent_null_diff applied to (P, n, M, M', V, y, T) with M' ⊆ M (`Set.inter_subset_left`), V open and y ∈ V yields HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' y T.
   (ii) (Q \ M') ∩ V ⊆ G \ M: if z ∈ Q, z ∉ M ∩ Q and z ∈ V, then z ∈ Q ∩ ball y r ⊆ G, and z ∉ M (otherwise z ∈ M ∩ Q). By E2, H^n ((Q \ M') ∩ V) = 0. `hasApproximateTangentSpaceAt_submodule` (finrank ℝ Q = n, y ∈ Q) gives HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (Q : Set (Euclid P)) y Q, and approx_tangent_null_diff applied to (P, n, Q, M', V, y, Q) with M' ⊆ Q (`Set.inter_subset_right`) yields HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' y Q.
   (iii) `HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique` applied to (i) and (ii) gives T = Q, so HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M y Q. By definition approxTangentPlane n M y = if h : ∃ Q', HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M y Q' then h.choose else ⊥; the condition holds (witness Q), so approxTangentPlane n M y = h.choose (`dite_eq_left`, the non-deprecated name of `dif_pos` on this toolchain), and h.choose_spec with `HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique` gives h.choose = Q.
   Hence y ∈ M ∧ θ y = k ∧ approxTangentPlane n M y = Q for H^n-a.e. y ∈ G. ∎
proof_key_steps: density_mult and the density hypothesis: Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ G lies in M with θ(y) = k; hence Hⁿ(G ∖ M) = 0.
R.orients (via ae_restrict_iff'): Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ M has an approximate tangent plane T; carrier_support_null: Hⁿ(M ∖ spt C) = 0.

Near such y, (M ∖ (M ∩ Q)) ∩ B_r(y) ⊆ M ∖ spt C and (Q ∖ (M ∩ Q)) ∩ B_r(y) ⊆ G ∖ M are null; approx_tangent_null_diff transfers T (from M) and Q (from Q, hasApproximateTangentSpaceAt_submodule) to M ∩ Q.
Uniqueness gives T = Q, and unfolding approxTangentPlane gives approxTangentPlane n M y = Q.

subproblems.title: The polar parametrization of an orthonormal pair pulls μHE[2]-null sets back to Lebesgue-null sets
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, a, e ∈ ℝ^P with |a| = |e| = 1 and ⟨a, e⟩ = 0, and let N ⊆ ℝ^P be an arbitrary set with μHE[2](N) = 0. Then for Lebesgue-almost every p = (t, α) ∈ ℝ × ℝ: if t > 0 and −π < α < π, then t(cos α·a + sin α·e) ∉ N.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (a e : Euclid P) (N : Set (Euclid P)), ‖a‖ = 1 → ‖e‖ = 1 → inner ℝ a e = 0 → μHE[2] N = 0 → ∀ᵐ p : ℝ × ℝ, 0 < p.1 → -Real.pi < p.2 → p.2 < Real.pi → p.1 • (Real.cos p.2 • a + Real.sin p.2 • e) ∉ N
subproblems.natural_proof:
1. (Isometric parametrization.) Define the ℝ-linear map ι : Euclid 2 →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid P, ι v := v 0 • a + v 1 • e. For v ∈ Euclid 2: ‖ι v‖² = (v 0)²‖a‖² + 2 (v 0)(v 1)⟨a, e⟩ + (v 1)²‖e‖² = (v 0)² + (v 1)² (`norm_add_sq_real`, `norm_smul`, `real_inner_smul_left`, `real_inner_smul_right`, ⟨a, e⟩ = 0, ‖a‖ = ‖e‖ = 1), and ‖v‖² = (v 0)² + (v 1)² (`EuclideanSpace.norm_eq`, `Real.sq_sqrt`, `Fin.sum_univ_two`). Both norms are ≥ 0, so ‖ι v‖ = ‖v‖ (`pow_left_inj₀`), and an additive norm-preserving map is an isometry (`AddMonoidHomClass.isometry_of_norm`).
2. (ι⁻¹ N is Lebesgue-null.) `Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_preimage` gives μHE[2] (ι ⁻¹' N) = μHE[2] (N ∩ range ι) ≤ μHE[2] N = 0 (`measure_mono_null`, `Set.inter_subset_left`), and μHE[2] = volume on Euclid 2 (`EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume 2`). So volume (ι ⁻¹' N) = 0.
3. (Pass to ℝ × ℝ.) Let κ : ℝ × ℝ → Euclid 2, κ p := WithLp.toLp 2 (MeasurableEquiv.finTwoArrow.symm p); then κ p 0 = p.1 and κ p 1 = p.2 (`MeasurableEquiv.finTwoArrow_symm_apply`). κ is measure preserving volume → volume, as the composition of `(volume_preserving_finTwoArrow ℝ).symm` and `PiLp.volume_preserving_toLp (Fin 2)`. Hence (`MeasurePreserving.quasiMeasurePreserving`, `QuasiMeasurePreserving.preimage_null`) N₃ := κ ⁻¹' (ι ⁻¹' N) has volume 0. Choose a measurable N₃' ⊇ N₃ with volume N₃' = 0 (`exists_measurable_superset_of_null`).
4. (Polar coordinates.) `lintegral_comp_polarCoord_symm` applied to f := N₃'.indicator 1 gives ∫⁻ p in polarCoord.target, ENNReal.ofReal p.1 • f (polarCoord.symm p) = ∫⁻ p, f p = volume N₃' = 0 (`lintegral_indicator_one`, N₃' measurable). The integrand is measurable (`ENNReal.measurable_ofReal.comp measurable_fst`, times the measurable indicator of N₃' composed with the continuous map polarCoord.symm, `continuous_polarCoord_symm`). By `lintegral_eq_zero_iff` it vanishes (volume.restrict polarCoord.target)-a.e.; polarCoord.target = Ioi 0 ×ˢ Ioo (−π) π is open, hence measurable, so `ae_restrict_iff'` gives: for volume-a.e. p, p ∈ polarCoord.target → ENNReal.ofReal p.1 • f (polarCoord.symm p) = 0.
5. (Conclusion.) Fix p as in Step 4 with 0 < p.1, −π < p.2 < π, so p ∈ polarCoord.target, and suppose p.1 • (cos p.2 • a + sin p.2 • e) ∈ N. Since polarCoord.symm p = (p.1 * cos p.2, p.1 * sin p.2) (`polarCoord_symm_apply`), ι (κ (polarCoord.symm p)) = (p.1 * cos p.2) • a + (p.1 * sin p.2) • e = p.1 • (cos p.2 • a + sin p.2 • e) (`smul_add`, `smul_smul`), so polarCoord.symm p ∈ N₃ ⊆ N₃'. Then the integrand at p is ENNReal.ofReal p.1 • 1 = ENNReal.ofReal p.1, which vanishes only if p.1 ≤ 0 (`ENNReal.ofReal_eq_zero`), contradicting 0 < p.1. Hence p.1 • (cos p.2 • a + sin p.2 • e) ∉ N. ∎
proof_key_steps: ι(v) = v₀a + v₁e is a linear isometry Euclid 2 → ℝ^P, so volume(ι⁻¹N) = μHE[2](N ∩ range ι) = 0.
κ : ℝ × ℝ → Euclid 2 (toLp ∘ finTwoArrow.symm) is measure preserving, so N₃ := κ⁻¹ι⁻¹N is Lebesgue-null; take a measurable null superset N₃'.
lintegral_comp_polarCoord_symm with the indicator of N₃': ∫_{target} ofReal(p₁)·1_{N₃'}(polarCoord.symm p) dp = 0, so the integrand vanishes a.e. on polarCoord.target.
On the target p₁ > 0, so polarCoord.symm p ∉ N₃', i.e. p₁(cos p₂·a + sin p₂·e) = ι(κ(polarCoord.symm p)) ∉ N.

subproblems.title: An open polar sector of angle at most π in the plane Q is relatively open in Q
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, Q a 2-dimensional linear subspace of ℝ^P, a, e ∈ Q with |a| = |e| = 1 and ⟨a, e⟩ = 0, and δ, t, φ ∈ ℝ with δ ≤ π, t > 0 and 0 < φ < δ. Then there is r > 0 such that every y ∈ Q with |y − t(cos φ·a + sin φ·e)| < r can be written y = t'(cos φ'·a + sin φ'·e) with t' > 0 and 0 < φ' < δ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (a e : Euclid P) (δ t φ : ℝ), Module.finrank ℝ Q = 2 → a ∈ Q → e ∈ Q → ‖a‖ = 1 → ‖e‖ = 1 → inner ℝ a e = 0 → δ ≤ Real.pi → 0 < t → 0 < φ → φ < δ → ∃ r : ℝ, 0 < r ∧ ∀ y : Euclid P, y ∈ Q → dist y (t • (Real.cos φ • a + Real.sin φ • e)) < r → ∃ t' φ' : ℝ, 0 < t' ∧ 0 < φ' ∧ φ' < δ ∧ y = t' • (Real.cos φ' • a + Real.sin φ' • e)
subproblems.natural_proof:
1. (Coordinates in Q.) The family ![a, e] is orthonormal (`orthonormal_iff_ite`, using ⟨a, a⟩ = ‖a‖² = 1, ⟨e, e⟩ = 1, ⟨a, e⟩ = ⟨e, a⟩ = 0), hence linearly independent. Its span is ≤ Q (`Submodule.span_le`; a, e ∈ Q) and has finrank 2 = finrank Q (`finrank_span_eq_card`), so Submodule.span ℝ (range ![a, e]) = Q (`Submodule.eq_of_le_of_finrank_eq`). For y ∈ Q, `Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun` and `Fin.sum_univ_two` give y = c 0 • a + c 1 • e; taking inner products with a and e gives ⟨y, a⟩ = c 0, ⟨y, e⟩ = c 1. Hence y = ⟨y, a⟩ • a + ⟨y, e⟩ • e for every y ∈ Q.
2. (An open set of coordinates.) Let W := Ioi 0 ×ˢ Ioo 0 δ ⊆ ℝ × ℝ (open). Since δ ≤ π and 0 < π, Ioo 0 δ ⊆ Ioo (−π) π, so W ⊆ polarCoord.target = Ioi 0 ×ˢ Ioo (−π) π. polarCoord.symm is an OpenPartialHomeomorph with source polarCoord.target, so O := polarCoord.symm '' W is open (`OpenPartialHomeomorph.isOpen_image_of_subset_source`).
3. (Continuous coordinates.) Let c : Euclid P → ℝ × ℝ, c y := (⟨y, a⟩, ⟨y, e⟩); it is continuous. For x₀ := t • (cos φ • a + sin φ • e), expanding with `inner_add_left`, `real_inner_smul_left` and the orthonormality relations gives c x₀ = (t * cos φ, t * sin φ) = polarCoord.symm (t, φ) with (t, φ) ∈ W (0 < t, 0 < φ < δ). So x₀ ∈ c ⁻¹' O, which is open, and `Metric.isOpen_iff` gives r > 0 with ball x₀ r ⊆ c ⁻¹' O.
4. (Conclusion.) Let y ∈ Q with dist y x₀ < r. Then c y ∈ O: there is (t', φ') ∈ W, i.e. 0 < t' and 0 < φ' < δ, with (t' * cos φ', t' * sin φ') = polarCoord.symm (t', φ') = c y, i.e. ⟨y, a⟩ = t' cos φ' and ⟨y, e⟩ = t' sin φ'. By Step 1, y = ⟨y, a⟩ • a + ⟨y, e⟩ • e = (t' * cos φ') • a + (t' * sin φ') • e = t' • (cos φ' • a + sin φ' • e) (`smul_add`, `smul_smul`). ∎
proof_key_steps: (a, e) is an orthonormal basis of Q, so y = ⟨y, a⟩a + ⟨y, e⟩e for every y ∈ Q.
W = (0, ∞) × (0, δ) ⊆ polarCoord.target (δ ≤ π), so O := polarCoord.symm '' W is open.
c(y) = (⟨y, a⟩, ⟨y, e⟩) is continuous and c(x₀) = polarCoord.symm (t, φ) ∈ O, giving a ball B_r(x₀) ⊆ c⁻¹(O).
For y ∈ Q ∩ B_r(x₀), c(y) = (t' cos φ', t' sin φ') with (t', φ') ∈ W, hence y = t'(cos φ'·a + sin φ'·e).

Accepted proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(3) (chapter-06.txt lines 763–767, printed without proof). It is the identity μ_T(W) = M_W(T) of Ch. 6, 2.7–2.8 (lines 264–282) for T = τ(M, θ, ξ), and it is the identity μ_T(B_ρ(x)) = M_{B_ρ(x)}(T) used in steps 2–4 of the parent proof.

Notation:
- H^n = μHE[n].
- μ := R.measure = θH^n⌞M, a Borel measure on ℝ^P that vanishes outside M ⊆ U and is finite on compact subsets of U (axiom locallyIntegrable_mult).
- For an n-covector α, |α| := (Σ_I α(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(n)})²)^{1/2}, summed over strictly increasing I : {1,…,n} → {1,…,P} (covectorEuclideanNorm). This is the Euclidean norm of the coefficient vector of α, hence a norm on n-covectors.
- ‖α‖ is the operator norm, and ⟨α, v⟩ := v(α) for an n-vector v.

Replace ξ by a Borel function that agrees with it H^n-a.e. on M. This changes neither the integral formula for T nor any a.e. statement below.

1. Linear algebra. Let τ₁, …, τ_n ∈ ℝ^P be orthonormal, τ_i = Σ_j A_{ij} e_j, and for strictly increasing I let A_I := (A_{i,I(k)})_{i,k}. Expand α(τ₁, …, τ_n) by multilinearity, drop the non-injective index maps (α is alternating), and group the injective ones by their image. This gives α(τ₁, …, τ_n) = Σ_I det(A_I) α(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(n)}). By the Cauchy–Binet formula, Σ_I det(A_I)² = det(AAᵀ) = det(⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩) = 1.
(a) By Cauchy–Schwarz, |α(τ₁, …, τ_n)| ≤ |α| for every α.
(b) Let J be the linear map sending an n-vector v to the n-covector J(v) with J(v)(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(n)}) = ⟨e^I, v⟩ for strictly increasing I. Here e^I := dx^{I(1)} ∧ ⋯ ∧ dx^{I(n)}, so e^I(v₁, …, v_n) = det(⟨e_{I(k)}, v_j⟩)_{k,j}. Suppose ⟨α, v⟩ = ε α(τ₁, …, τ_n) for all α, with ε ∈ {1, −1}. Then ⟨e^I, v⟩ = ε det(A_I), so |J(v)| = (Σ_I det(A_I)²)^{1/2} = 1 and ⟨J(v), v⟩ = ε J(v)(τ₁, …, τ_n) = ε² Σ_I det(A_I)² = 1.
For n = 0 these facts are immediate: α(τ) = α(()) and |α| = |α(())|.
By the axiom orients of R (IsUnitOrientationOf), ξ(x) has this form for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M, hence for μ-a.e. x. Therefore, μ-a.e.: |⟨α, ξ(x)⟩| ≤ |α| for every α, and β(x) := J(ξ(x)) satisfies |β(x)| = 1 and ⟨β(x), ξ(x)⟩ = 1. The map β = J∘ξ is Borel.

2. M_W(T) ≤ μ(W). Let ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with spt ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. The integrand θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ vanishes off the compact set K := spt ω ⊆ U. By step 1 it is bounded in absolute value by θ1_{M∩K} H^n-a.e. on M, which is integrable. Hence T(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dH^n ≤ ∫_{M∩W} θ|ω| dH^n ≤ μ(W). The zero form is admissible, so M_W(T) = sup ENNReal.ofReal(T(ω)) ≤ μ(W).

3. Choice of K and V. Let λ be real with 0 ≤ λ < μ(W); it suffices to find an admissible ω with T(ω) > λ.
- The sets W_j := {y ∈ W : |y| < j, dist(y, ℝ^P ∖ W) > 1/j} increase to W and have compact closures W̄_j ⊆ W. By continuity from below, μ(K) > λ for K := W̄_j with j large, and μ(K) < ∞ because K is a compact subset of U.
- Fix ε > 0 with μ(K) > λ + 3ε.
- Pick d > 0 with K₁ := {y : dist(y, K) ≤ d} ⊆ W. Since K₁ is compact, μ⌞K₁ is a finite Borel measure on ℝ^P, hence outer regular, so there is an open V' ⊇ K with μ(K₁ ∩ V' ∖ K) < ε.
- Put V := V' ∩ {y : dist(y, K) < d}. Then V is open, K ⊆ V, V̄ ⊆ K₁ ⊆ W, and μ(V ∖ K) < ε.

4. A smooth admissible form.
- β is Borel with |β| = 1 μ-a.e., so β ∈ L¹(μ⌞K). Continuous compactly supported maps are dense in L¹ of the finite Borel (hence regular) measure μ⌞K on ℝ^P, so there is a continuous compactly supported g with ∫_K |g − β| dμ < ε.
- Let π(α) := α / max(1, |α|), the nearest-point retraction onto the closed unit ball of the Euclidean norm |·|; π is 1-Lipschitz. Then g₁ := π∘g is continuous and compactly supported, |g₁| ≤ 1, and |g₁ − β| = |π(g) − π(β)| ≤ |g − β| μ-a.e. on K.
- With a standard mollifier φ_δ ≥ 0, ∫φ_δ = 1, put g₂ := g₁ * φ_δ (coefficientwise). Then g₂ is C^∞, and |g₂(x)| ≤ ∫ |g₁(x − y)| φ_δ(y) dy ≤ 1 because |·| is a norm. Also g₂ → g₁ uniformly as δ ↓ 0 because g₁ is uniformly continuous; fix δ with sup |g₂ − g₁| ≤ ε/(μ(K) + 1).
- Choose χ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^P) with 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, χ = 1 on K and spt χ ⊆ V (smooth Urysohn lemma), and set ω := χ g₂.
Then ω is smooth with compact support, spt ω ⊆ V ⊆ W ⊆ U, and |ω| = χ|g₂| ≤ 1. So ω is admissible for M_W(T).

5. Estimate. We have ω = g₂ on K and ω = 0 off V. By step 1, μ-a.e. |⟨α, ξ⟩| ≤ |α| and ⟨β, ξ⟩ = 1. As μ = θH^n⌞M:
T(ω) = ∫ ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ = ∫_K ⟨g₂, ξ⟩ dμ + ∫_{V∖K} ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ
≥ ∫_K ⟨β, ξ⟩ dμ − ∫_K |g₂ − β| dμ − μ(V ∖ K)
≥ μ(K) − (∫_K |g₂ − g₁| dμ + ∫_K |g₁ − β| dμ) − ε
> μ(K) − 3ε > λ.

6. Conclusion. By step 5, M_W(T) ≥ ENNReal.ofReal(T(ω)) > λ for every real λ ∈ [0, μ(W)). So M_W(T) ≥ μ(W), and with step 2, M_W(T) = μ(W). If n > P, then H^n = 0 on ℝ^P, so μ = 0, T = 0 and both sides vanish; step 3 is then vacuous.
proof_key_steps: Cauchy–Binet: |α(τ₁,…,τ_n)| ≤ |α| for orthonormal τ, and J(ξ) is a unit covector with ⟨J(ξ), ξ⟩ = 1.
Upper bound M_W(T) ≤ ∫_{M∩W} θ dH^n from the integral formula.
Lower bound: inner and outer regularity, L¹-density of continuous maps, radial retraction, mollification and a cut-off give an admissible ω with T(ω) > μ(K) − 3ε > λ.

subproblems.title: The mass density of an integer multiplicity current equals its multiplicity almost everywhere
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity representation of T in U (an IMRep with R.Represents T), with weight μ_T = R.measure = θH^n⌞M. Accepted proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 4, p. 91 (chapter-04.txt line 350: Θ^n(V, x) = θ(x) for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M, by Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(2)). This is Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(1)–(2) with Theorem 1.9 (chapter-03.txt lines 298–325), the fact used in step 2 of the parent proof. The argument uses two ingredients:
- the approximate tangent planes supplied by R (Ch. 3, Definition 1.4 and Remark 1.5(3), lines 77–101);
- the Lebesgue differentiation theorem for Radon measures (Ch. 1, Corollary 3.17 with Remark 3.11(3), chapter-01.txt lines 773–960), which is the content of Remark 1.8(1).

Notation: H^n = μHE[n], μ := H^n⌞M, ν := R.measure = θμ, ω_n := unitBallVolume n; B_ρ(x) is the open ball and B̄_ρ(x) the closed ball.

1. Local finiteness. For compact K ⊆ U: μ(K) = H^n(M ∩ K) ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dH^n < ∞ (θ ≥ 1 on M), and ν(K) < ∞.

2. Unweighted density (Remark 1.5(3)). By the axiom orients of R, for μ-a.e. x there is an n-dimensional subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q. That is, ∫_{η_{x,ρ}(M)} f dH^n → ∫_Q f dH^n as ρ ↓ 0 for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), where η_{x,ρ}(y) = ρ^{−1}(y − x).
Fix such an x ∈ M ⊆ U, s > 0 with B̄_s(x) ⊆ U, and 0 < ε < 1. Choose f₁, f₂ ∈ C_c(ℝ^P; [0, 1]) with:
- f₁ = 1 on B̄_{1−ε}(0) and spt f₁ ⊆ B_1(0);
- f₂ = 1 on B̄_1(0) and spt f₂ ⊆ B_{1+ε}(0).
H^n is translation invariant and H^n(ρ^{−1}A) = ρ^{−n}H^n(A) (Mathlib euclideanHausdorffMeasure_homothety_image). Also η_{x,ρ}(M) ∩ B_t(0) = η_{x,ρ}(M ∩ B_{tρ}(x)). Hence for 0 < ρ < s/2:
∫_{η_{x,ρ}(M)} f₁ dH^n ≤ ρ^{−n}μ(B_ρ(x)) ≤ ρ^{−n}μ(B̄_ρ(x)) ≤ ∫_{η_{x,ρ}(M)} f₂ dH^n,
all finite by step 1. H^n⌞Q is n-dimensional Lebesgue measure carried by a linear isometry ℝ^n ≅ Q (Mathlib Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image). So ∫_Q f₁ dH^n ≥ H^n(Q ∩ B̄_{1−ε}(0)) = ω_n(1 − ε)^n and ∫_Q f₂ dH^n ≤ H^n(Q ∩ B_{1+ε}(0)) = ω_n(1 + ε)^n.
Letting ρ ↓ 0 and then ε ↓ 0 gives μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρ^n) → 1 and μ(B̄_ρ(x))/(ω_nρ^n) → 1. In particular μ(B̄_ρ(x)) > 0 for small ρ > 0.
Edge cases: for n = 0, Q = {0}, H^0 is counting measure, ω_0 = 1 and ρ^0 = 1, and the same computation applies. If n > P, then H^n = 0 on ℝ^P, ν = 0 and the statement is vacuous.

3. Lebesgue differentiation.
- Let K_j := {y : |y| ≤ j, dist(y, ℝ^P ∖ U) ≥ 1/j}. Each K_j is a compact subset of U whose interior contains {y : |y| < j, dist(y, ℝ^P ∖ U) > 1/j}, so U = ⋃_j int K_j.
- The measures μ_j := μ⌞K_j and ν_j := ν⌞K_j = θμ_j are finite (step 1), and dν_j/dμ_j = θ μ_j-a.e.
- By the Besicovitch differentiation theorem (Ch. 1, 3.17 with 3.11(3); Mathlib Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_rnDeriv) there is Z_j with μ_j(Z_j) = 0, i.e. μ(Z_j ∩ K_j) = 0, such that ν_j(B̄_ρ(x))/μ_j(B̄_ρ(x)) → θ(x) as ρ ↓ 0 for every x ∉ Z_j.
- Let E := ⋃_j (Z_j ∩ K_j) ∪ E₂, where E₂ is the μ-null exceptional set of step 2. Then μ(E) = 0.
- Let x ∈ M ∖ E and choose j with x ∈ int K_j; then x ∉ Z_j. For 0 < ρ < dist(x, ℝ^P ∖ int K_j) we have B̄_ρ(x) ⊆ K_j, so μ_j(B̄_ρ(x)) = μ(B̄_ρ(x)) and ν_j(B̄_ρ(x)) = ν(B̄_ρ(x)).
Hence ν(B̄_ρ(x))/(ω_nρ^n) = [ν(B̄_ρ(x))/μ(B̄_ρ(x))]·[μ(B̄_ρ(x))/(ω_nρ^n)] → θ(x)·1 = θ(x).

subproblems.title: Euclidean density comparison: a lower n-density bound controls μHE[n]
subproblems.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ and c > 0 real. There is a constant C ∈ [0, ∞), depending only on N, n and c, with the following property. Let ν be any measure on ℝ^N = Euclid N with its Borel σ-algebra, O ⊆ ℝ^N an open set, and A ⊆ O. Suppose each x ∈ A admits t₀ > 0 such that ν(B̄_t(x)) ≥ c tⁿ for all t ∈ (0, t₀), where B̄_t(x) is the closed ball and the inequality is read in [0, ∞] as ENNReal.ofReal(c tⁿ) ≤ ν(B̄_t(x)). Then Hⁿ(A) ≤ C·ν(O), where Hⁿ = μHE[n] is Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure on ℝ^N, evaluated as an outer measure on the arbitrary set A.

This is the off-carrier half of the density identification in step 2 of the parent proof.

Accepted proof:
**Source:** step 4 of the parent proof and its library-glue note. That is Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 1, Theorem 3.3 (printed p. 14; book/chapter-01.txt line 602): if μ is Borel regular, A₁ ⊆ A₂ and Θ*ⁿ(μ, A₂, x) ≥ t for x ∈ A₁, then t Hⁿ(A₁) ≤ μ(A₂). The comparison is applied to the outer measure of ν. A positive normalization constant replaces 1, which the parent's note allows. Notation: E := ℝ^N = Euclid N, B(x, ρ) is the open ball and B̄_r(x) the closed ball.

**Library facts used.** They come from the pinned simongmt package, namespace Poincare.SimonGMT. The Lean implementation adds `import Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter01.DensityComparison` and `import Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.AreaNormalization` to GMT/Ch07/Submission.lean; the frozen contract still elaborates with these imports.
- **(L1)** ω := Chapter01.realUnitBallVolume (n : ℝ) satisfies 0 < ω < ∞, by `realUnitBallVolume_pos (Nat.cast_nonneg n)` and `realUnitBallVolume_ne_top`.
- **(L2)** s := Chapter02.simonAreaNormalization n satisfies 0 < s < ∞, by `simonAreaNormalization_pos` and `simonAreaNormalization_ne_top`.
  - Simon's Hausdorff measure on E satisfies Chapter01.simonHausdorffMeasureReal (n : ℝ) = s • μHE[n], by `simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_smul_euclideanHausdorffMeasure`.
  - Its outer measure is Chapter01.simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal (n : ℝ), by `simonHausdorffMeasureReal_toOuterMeasure` with 0 ≤ (n : ℝ).
- **(L3)** For an outer measure μ' on E, a set A₂ and x ∈ E, the upper density is Θ*ⁿ(μ', A₂, x) = limsup over r → 0⁺ (filter 𝓝[>] 0) of μ'(A₂ ∩ B̄_r(x)) / (ω · ofReal(r)^(n:ℝ)). In Lean these are `Chapter01.dimensionalUpperDensity` and `dimensionalDensityQuotient`.
- **(L4)** Simon 3.3 (`Chapter01.simon_theorem_3_3`): let μ' be a Borel regular outer measure on a metric space, 0 ≤ n, A₁ ⊆ A₂ and t ≥ 0 real. If ofReal t ≤ Θ*ⁿ(μ', A₂, x) for every x ∈ A₁, then ofReal t · simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal n (A₁) ≤ μ'(A₂).
- **(L5)** For any measure ν on the Borel space E, the outer measure μ' := ν.toOuterMeasure is Borel regular (`Chapter01.measure_toOuterMeasure_isBorelRegular`) and agrees with ν on every set.

**Proof.**

1. **The constant.** Put τ := c / ω.toReal. By (L1), ω.toReal > 0, so τ > 0 and ofReal τ > 0. Define C := (ofReal τ · s)⁻¹. By (L2) and ofReal τ > 0, the product ofReal τ · s is nonzero, so C ≠ ∞. C depends only on n and c.

2. **Setup.** Fix ν, A and O as in the statement and let μ' := ν.toOuterMeasure, which is Borel regular by (L5).

3. **Density lower bound.** Let x ∈ A and take t₀ > 0 from the hypothesis. O is open and x ∈ A ⊆ O, so there is ρ > 0 with B(x, ρ) ⊆ O. Let r ∈ (0, min(t₀, ρ)).
   - (a) B̄_r(x) ⊆ B(x, ρ) ⊆ O, hence O ∩ B̄_r(x) = B̄_r(x).
   - (b) ofReal(r)^(n:ℝ) = ofReal(r)^n = ofReal(rⁿ), by `ENNReal.rpow_natCast` and `ENNReal.ofReal_pow` with r ≥ 0. Also rⁿ > 0, so 0 < ω · ofReal(rⁿ) < ∞.
   - (c) Since ω ≠ ∞ we have ω = ofReal(ω.toReal), and τ · ω.toReal = c. So ofReal(τ) · (ω · ofReal(rⁿ)) = ofReal(τ · ω.toReal · rⁿ) = ofReal(c rⁿ) ≤ ν(B̄_r(x)), by the hypothesis at t = r ∈ (0, t₀).
   - (d) The density quotient at radius r is μ'(O ∩ B̄_r(x)) / (ω · ofReal(r)^(n:ℝ)) = ν(B̄_r(x)) / (ω · ofReal(rⁿ)). By (c) and the ENNReal rule a ≤ b/d ⇔ a·d ≤ b for 0 < d < ∞ (`ENNReal.le_div_iff_mul_le`), this quotient is ≥ ofReal τ.
   - (e) The interval (0, min(t₀, ρ)) belongs to 𝓝[>] 0, so the inequality holds eventually, hence frequently, since 𝓝[>] 0 is nontrivial. Therefore Θ*ⁿ(μ', O, x) = limsup of the quotient ≥ ofReal τ (`Filter.le_limsup_of_frequently_le`; the coboundedness side condition is automatic in [0, ∞]).

   So ofReal τ ≤ Θ*ⁿ(μ', O, x) for every x ∈ A.

4. **Comparison.** Apply (L4) with μ', n := (n : ℝ) ≥ 0, A₁ := A, A₂ := O (A ⊆ O) and t := τ ≥ 0. This gives ofReal τ · simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal (n : ℝ) (A) ≤ μ'(O) = ν(O).

5. **Normalization.** By (L2), simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal (n : ℝ) (A) = simonHausdorffMeasureReal (n : ℝ) (A) = s · μHE[n](A). Hence (ofReal τ · s) · μHE[n](A) ≤ ν(O).

6. **Division.** Since 0 < ofReal τ · s < ∞, step 5 is equivalent to μHE[n](A) ≤ ν(O) / (ofReal τ · s) = (ofReal τ · s)⁻¹ · ν(O) = C · ν(O), by `ENNReal.le_div_iff_mul_le` and `ENNReal.div_eq_inv_mul`. This is the claim, with the finite constant C from step 1. ∎
proof_key_steps: Let ω = realUnitBallVolume n ∈ (0, ∞) and s = simonAreaNormalization n ∈ (0, ∞). Set τ := c/ω.toReal > 0 and C := (ofReal τ · s)⁻¹, which is finite.
For x ∈ A, small closed balls B̄_r(x) lie in the open set O. The bound ν(B̄_r(x)) ≥ c rⁿ makes every small-radius density quotient ≥ τ, so Θ*ⁿ(ν, O, x) ≥ τ.
simon_theorem_3_3, applied to the Borel regular outer measure of ν with A₁ = A and A₂ = O, gives τ · H_S^n(A) ≤ ν(O).
Since H_S^n = s · μHE[n], dividing by the positive finite number τ·s gives μHE[n](A) ≤ C · ν(O).

subproblems.title: Small open neighbourhoods of a null set at which the measure is locally finite
subproblems.statement: Let N ∈ ℕ and let μ be a measure on ℝ^N = Euclid N with its Borel σ-algebra; for an arbitrary set S ⊆ ℝ^N, μ(S) denotes the outer measure. Let A ⊆ ℝ^N with μ(A) = 0, and suppose every x ∈ A has some r > 0 with μ(B(x, r)) < ∞, where B(x, r) is the open ball. Then for every ε ∈ (0, ∞] there is an open set O ⊆ ℝ^N with A ⊆ O and μ(O) < ε.

It supplies open sets O ⊇ A of arbitrarily small R.measure, for the R.measure-null set A of off-carrier points, at whose points R.measure is locally finite.

Accepted proof:
**Source:** step 3 of the parent proof (localized outer regularity). The parent's exhaustion of W by sets V_j is replaced by a countable cover of A by open balls of finite μ-measure; this is the same argument. Notation: E := ℝ^N = Euclid N, B(x, r) is the open ball, and N, μ, A are as in the statement. Fix ε ∈ (0, ∞], so ε ≠ 0.

1. **Choice of radii.** For each x ∈ A choose r(x) > 0 with μ(B(x, r(x))) < ∞. This uses the hypothesis and choice; in Lean, `choose! r hr hfin using hloc`.

2. **Countable subcover.** The sets B(x, r(x)), x ∈ A, are open, and E is second countable. By the Lindelöf property (Lean: `TopologicalSpace.isOpen_iUnion_countable` for the family indexed by the subtype of A) there is a countable T ⊆ A with ⋃_{i∈T} B(i, r(i)) = ⋃_{x∈A} B(x, r(x)). Write B_i := B(i, r(i)) for i ∈ T. Each x ∈ A lies in its own ball B(x, r(x)) because r(x) > 0. Hence A ⊆ ⋃_{x∈A} B(x, r(x)) = ⋃_{i∈T} B_i.

3. **Error budget.** T is countable and ε ≠ 0, so there are real numbers ε_i > 0 (i ∈ T) with Σ_{i∈T} ε_i < ε. In Lean: `ENNReal.exists_pos_sum_of_countable` applied to the countable type T.

4. **Local approximation.** Fix i ∈ T and let μ_i := μ⌞B_i (Lean `μ.restrict B_i`).
   - (a) μ_i(E) = μ(B_i) < ∞ by step 1. So μ_i is a finite Borel measure on the metric space E, hence outer regular. In Mathlib, `Measure.WeaklyRegular.of_pseudoMetrizableSpace_of_isFiniteMeasure` gives weak regularity, and weakly regular measures are outer regular.
   - (b) The restriction satisfies μ_i ≤ μ setwise (`Measure.restrict_le_self`). Hence μ_i(A ∩ B_i) ≤ μ_i(A) ≤ μ(A) = 0 < ε_i.
   - (c) By outer regularity (`Set.exists_isOpen_lt_of_lt` applied to the set A ∩ B_i and the bound ε_i) there is an open O_i ⊇ A ∩ B_i with μ_i(O_i) < ε_i.
   - (d) O_i is open, hence measurable, so μ_i(O_i) = μ(O_i ∩ B_i) (`Measure.restrict_apply`). Thus μ(O_i ∩ B_i) < ε_i.

5. **Definition of O.** Put O := ⋃_{i∈T} (O_i ∩ B_i). Each O_i ∩ B_i is an intersection of two open sets, hence open, so O is open.

6. **A ⊆ O.** Let x ∈ A. By step 2 there is i ∈ T with x ∈ B_i. Then x ∈ A ∩ B_i ⊆ O_i, so x ∈ O_i ∩ B_i ⊆ O.

7. **Measure bound.** By countable subadditivity (`measure_iUnion_le`), then step 4(d) termwise (`ENNReal.tsum_le_tsum`), then step 3: μ(O) ≤ Σ_{i∈T} μ(O_i ∩ B_i) ≤ Σ_{i∈T} ε_i < ε. If A = ∅, the same computation applies: T may be empty, O = ∅ and μ(O) = 0 < ε.

8. **Conclusion.** O is open, A ⊆ O and μ(O) < ε, as required. ∎
proof_key_steps: Around each x ∈ A choose an open ball B(x, r(x)) of finite μ-measure.
Second countability (Lindelöf) gives a countable subfamily (B_i)_{i∈T} whose union contains A.
Choose positive budgets ε_i with Σ_{i∈T} ε_i < ε.
The finite measure μ⌞B_i is outer regular. Since μ⌞B_i(A ∩ B_i) = 0, there is an open O_i ⊇ A ∩ B_i with μ(O_i ∩ B_i) < ε_i.
O := ⋃_i (O_i ∩ B_i) is open and contains A, and subadditivity gives μ(O) ≤ Σ ε_i < ε.

subproblems.title: An integer multiplicity representation carries no H^n-mass off the support of the current
subproblems.statement: Let P, n be natural numbers, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (a GeometricCurrentOn U n) and R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep U n) representing T, i.e. T(ω) = ∫_M θ ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dH^n for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U). Then H^n(M ∖ spt T) = 0, where spt T = U ∖ ⋃{W : W open, closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U, T vanishes on W} (Simon 6.2.11).

Accepted proof:
Source: this is the fact "μ_T(U ∖ spt T) = 0", used in step 2 of the parent proof (Simon 6.2.11 with 6.3.1; μ_T = θH^n⌞M by 6.3.2(3)).
1. Notation. M := R.carrier ⊆ U, θ := R.mult (θ ≥ 1 on M), ξ := R.orient, μ := μHE[n].restrict M. By definition T.support = U ∖ Z with Z := T.zeroRegion = ⋃𝒲, where 𝒲 is the family of open W with closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U and T.VanishesOn W (T ω = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W). Since M ⊆ U, M ∖ T.support = M ∩ Z.
2. Countable reduction. ℝ^P is second countable, so ⋃𝒲 = ⋃_k W_k for a countable subfamily (W_k) ⊆ 𝒲 (Mathlib TopologicalSpace.isOpen_sUnion_countable). By countable subadditivity it suffices to show H^n(M ∩ W) = 0 for one fixed W ∈ 𝒲.
3. A finite measure. C := closure W is compact and C ⊆ U, so ∫_{M ∩ C} θ dH^n < ∞ by R.locallyIntegrable_mult; since θ ≥ 1 on M, H^n(M ∩ C) < ∞. Put ν := μHE[n].restrict (M ∩ C), a finite Borel measure on ℝ^P.
4. Orientation facts. By R.orients, for μ-a.e. x there are a plane Q and an orthonormal family τ = (τ_1, …, τ_n) spanning Q with ξ(x)(β) = s·β(τ_1, …, τ_n) for all n-covectors β, s ∈ {1, −1}. At such x: (a) |ξ(x)(β)| ≤ ‖β‖ (operator norm of the continuous alternating map, since |τ_i| = 1); (b) ξ(x) ≠ 0: the n-covector β_τ(u_1, …, u_n) := det(⟨τ_a, u_b⟩)_{a,b} (for n = 0 the constant 1) is continuous, multilinear and alternating, and β_τ(τ) = det I = 1, so ξ(x)(β_τ) = s ≠ 0.
5. Testing T. Fix an n-covector α and set f_α(x) := θ(x)·ξ(x)(α). It is ν-a.e. strongly measurable (θ measurable, ξ a.e. strongly measurable for μ ≥ ν) and |f_α| ≤ ‖α‖θ ν-a.e., so f_α ∈ L¹(ν). For every g ∈ C^∞(ℝ^P, ℝ) with compact support and tsupport g ⊆ W, the form ω(x) := g(x)·α is smooth with compact support and tsupport ω ⊆ tsupport g ⊆ W ⊆ U, so ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport in W. As T vanishes on W and R represents T: 0 = T ω = ∫_M θ(x) ξ(x)(g(x)α) dH^n = ∫ g f_α dν (the integrand vanishes off W ⊆ C).
6. Fundamental lemma. Mathlib's IsOpen.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero (open set W, measure ν, f_α locally integrable on W) gives: for ν-a.e. x, x ∈ W ⇒ θ(x)ξ(x)(α) = 0. Since θ ≥ 1 on M and ν is carried by M, ξ(x)(α) = 0 for ν-a.e. x ∈ W.
7. Conclusion. Let α_1, …, α_m be a basis of the finite-dimensional space of n-covectors on ℝ^P. Intersecting the finitely many full-measure sets of step 6, for ν-a.e. x ∈ W the linear functional ξ(x) vanishes on a basis, hence ξ(x) = 0. By step 4(b), ξ(x) ≠ 0 for μ-a.e. x, hence for ν-a.e. x. Therefore ν(W) = H^n(M ∩ C ∩ W) = H^n(M ∩ W) = 0, and by step 2, H^n(M ∖ T.support) = 0.
proof_key_steps: M ∖ spt T = M ∩ zeroRegion(T), a countable union of open W ⊂⊂ U on which T vanishes.
Testing T with g·α (g ∈ C_c^∞(W), α a constant covector) gives ∫ g θ ξ(α) dH^n⌞M = 0.
The fundamental lemma of the calculus of variations gives ξ = 0 a.e. on M ∩ W, while unit orientations are nonzero; hence H^n(M ∩ W) = 0.
